newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent firmer Monday based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.
Friday, benchmark December settled 0.03 cent weaker at 75.60 cents a lb after trading from 75.90 to 75.33 cents. The rest ended 0.03 to 0.10 cent lower.
The October/December spread closed at 0.15 cent.

Analysts expect the market to remain rangebound and volume thin amid a lack of fundamental news. Conditions across the cotton belt are favorable for the developing crop, which is growing slightly behind schedule in the Delta and Southeast, Weather Services Corp said.
Players await the USDA's monthly supply and demand estimates due for Aug 12 release. The report contains the the first survey-based estimates of the season.
Technical support remains at 74.00 cents followed by 72.00 cents for most-active December delivery.
